label: Microbial
note: Mats and films. Half its colour is the pigment it uses, half is the ground it grows on.

label: Fungal
note: Mostly not photosynthetic, so mostly not the colour of its star. The tint list is deliberately wide — Earth's own surface-colouring fungal-ish organism is lichen, and lichen runs from near-black to bright orange.

label: Flora
note: An empty tint list and full pigment drive: flora is the colour of what its pigment reflects, and nothing else. Its lack of lights is an EMPTY LIGHT RANGE here, not a rule in the code.

label: Fauna
note: Animals do not tint a world seen from orbit. That is TWO EMPTY RANGES in this record — no tints, no pigment drive — not a special case anywhere in the code.

label: Technological
note: Dark by day, lit by night. It needed no code: a dark tint range and a strong light range, in the same record shape as everything else. This is the extensibility test — a sixth morphology is another entry here.
